code.codeC:
Kernel-ratio completeness in darksirens (completion.py, consumed by prior.py)

GRID AND SMOOTHING OPERATOR
All quantities live on the package zgrid (zmax = zgrid[-1]). One Gaussian kernel width _SIGMA_SMOOTH = 0.05 is used for BOTH sides of the ratio. The observed-galaxy KDE (_kde_dndz_obs) gives, per pixel/row,

  dN_obs_s(z|pix) = Σ_{i in pix, real} N(z; z_i, σ) / M(z_i),  M(z_i) = Φ((zmax−z_i)/σ) − Φ(−z_i/σ)

i.e. each real galaxy contributes a unit-mass truncated-renormalized Gaussian; raw counts, no luminosity weights (wgals/ngals only mask padded slots). M floored at 1e-300. The matching linear operator S (_build_smoothing_operator, (N_grid,N_grid), built once at import; threaded through jit boundaries via a contextvar) applies the identical per-source-point kernel to any grid function via trapezoid quadrature: (S f)(z_g) = ∫ N(z_g; z', σ)/M(z') f(z') dz'. Because the operator is linear and shared, a constant true completeness passes through the ratio exactly, including at z = 0; there is no parametric roll-off — survey depth appears as the data-driven decline of dN_obs_s.

EXPECTED COUNTS (sky-aggregate, per-pixel amplitude)
g(z) = dV_c/dz (1+z)^delta (exponent delta, not delta−1; log floored at 1e-300 so g(0)=0 stays finite in log). Then (_precompute_grids, once per proposal, pixel-INDEPENDENT):

  dN_exp(z) = n0 · apix · g(z),   dN_exp_smooth = S @ dN_exp.

Note dN_exp is ISOTROPIC: the same curve for every pixel (n0, apix, cosmology, delta only).

PER-PIXEL COMPLETENESS (_row_C)
  C(z|pix) = clip( dN_obs_s(z|pix) / max-guard(dN_exp_smooth), 0, 1 ),
with the denominator guarded as where(dN_exp_smooth > 0, dN_exp_smooth, 1). The ONLY per-pixel input is the KDE numerator (cached row-for-row in EMCatalog.dN_obs_kde via build_pixel_kde_cache; cache row == catalog row, so it is indexed directly by row, pinned by tests/test_cache_row_indexing.py). Empty pixels have dN_obs_s ≡ 0 ⇒ C ≡ 0. Clipping at 1 is the only place overdense pixels are suppressed.

MISSING BRANCH (_assemble_curves)
  dN_miss(z|pix) = (1 − C(z|pix)) · dN_exp(z) · lss(pix, z),
where lss is either the legacy factor max(1 + b_eff·δ_g(pix,z), 0), b_eff = alpha_miss·b_miss (exactly degenerate product; only b_miss sampled), or a precomputed Q_LSS row (clip of logQ to ±7 then exp; Q REPLACES the δ_g factor, is never renormalized; ensemble members handled cube-free via base_miss = (1−C)·dN_exp with per-member Q_eff). δ_g comes from compute_lss_overdensity: per-pixel KDE minus the mean over OCCUPIED pixels, divided by that mean; δ_g = 0 for empty pixels and wherever the mean vanishes — so angular clustering of the missing branch currently enters ONLY through this factor, not through C or dN_exp. N_miss = ∫ dN_miss dz (full-grid trapezoid). Diagnostics: C_eff = clip(1 − dN_miss/dN_exp, 0, 1) (denominator guarded), f = 1 − N_miss/N_exp.

Z_DEPTH: a concrete Python float (trace-time branch, no mask when None). For z > z_depth: C := 0 and lss := 1, i.e. dN_miss := dN_exp there (hosts missing, not nonexistent — the prior above the depth is the plain volumetric×population shape, NOT zero). N_miss, C_eff (=0 beyond depth), and f still use the full grid. In the ensemble path Q_eff is forced to 1 beyond the depth.

OBSERVED BRANCH AND ASSEMBLY (prior.py, dark_sirens model)
  p(z|pix) = [ N_obs(pix) · p_cat(z|pix) + dN_miss(z|pix) ] / [ N_obs(pix) + N_miss(pix) ],
with p_cat the per-pixel normalized weighted-kernel catalog shape (catalog.py), N_obs the real-galaxy COUNT (missing population gets the pixel-mean observed weight; catalog:missing odds are count odds). Integrates to 1 per pixel by construction; empty pixels route automatically to the missing branch (N_obs = 0). With z_depth, the observed amplitude becomes N_obs·exp(log_depth_mass) (below-depth kernel-mass fraction). prepare_redshift_prior_state calls completion_curves once per proposal (O(N_rows×N_grid)); per-sample eval is a row gather + interpolation, behind an optimization barrier.

FIELD CONVENTION (sky-aggregate normalizer)
field_global_log_Z replaces the per-pixel denominator by the GLOBAL Z(θ) = Σ_all-pix [N_obs,pix + N_miss,pix(θ)], accumulating the curve V(z) = Σ_occ (1−C_p)·lss_p + V_empty (empty pixels contribute n_empty, or Σ_empty Q_p in Q mode) then integrating dN_exp·V once. C is recomputed there from float32 full-sky KDE rows (field_dN_obs_s) with the identical clip/guard recipe; beyond z_depth V relaxes to the total pixel count, and the observed term is the depth-scaled Σ_pix N_obs,pix·m_pix(θ) (per-galaxy Z_depth/Z ratios, f64) to avoid double-counting above-depth catalogued galaxies.

WHAT IS PER-PIXEL vs AGGREGATE (redesign-relevant)
Per-pixel: dN_obs_s (hence C), δ_g rows, Q_LSS rows, N_obs, p_cat. Sky-aggregate/isotropic: n0, apix, g(z), dN_exp, dN_exp_smooth, S, σ_smooth, z_depth. So C already absorbs angular clustering of the OBSERVED galaxies (numerator per-pixel, denominator isotropic mean) — an overdense complete pixel reads C > 1 and is clipped to 1, silently discarding its excess; the missing branch's clustering is reinstated only multiplicatively via lss. Clips/floors: C∈[0,1], lss ≥ 0, |logQ| ≤ 7, kernel-mass/g/Z floors at 1e-300, guarded denominators; completion_clip_diagnostics reports per-pixel clipped fractions.

code.codeQ:
Q-table construction in /hildafs/projects/phy230014p/magana/src/darksirens-dev/darksirens/redshift/lognormal_completion.py (with hyperparameter plumbing from darksirens/cli/build_lognormal_completion.py and darksirens/core/types.py):

PURPOSE. Offline builder of the LSS-conditioned completion field Q_LSS(p,z) consumed by darksirens.redshift.completion. Never imported by the GW likelihood; the likelihood consumes fixed logQ arrays (EMCatalog.lss_completion_*).

RADIAL MODE (mode="radial"): per-pixel 1-D Poisson-lognormal fit. Per occupied HEALPix pixel, independently, a latent Gaussian field s on the redshift grid with stationary Gaussian correlation, represented by circulant FFT eigenvalues P (gaussian_correlation_spectrum: c[d]=sigma^2 exp(-d^2/2 ell^2) on periodic grid-index distance, P=Re fft(c), floored at 1e-8 of max; sigma_s^2 = mean(P) = c[0]). Observed binned counts are Poisson: N_obs_v ~ Poisson(lambda_v), lambda_v = C_v * dN_exp_v * exp(b s_v - shift), with mean-one shift = 0.5 b^2 sigma_s^2 / prior_strength (the /ps divisor is documented as essential: the effective prior variance is sigma2/ps, and omitting it made a data-free bin read Q<1, ~31% suppression at ps=4). MAP minimizes 0.5*ps*s^T C^{-1} s + sum_v [lambda_v - N_obs_v log lambda_v], all algebra in Fourier space (no dense covariance). Solver: L-BFGS-B, maxiter=200000, maxfun=21*maxiter (documented fix: scipy's default maxfun=15000 silently capped DESI-scale solves; earlier maxiter=300 under-relaxed logQ ~5x toward Q=1). The output table is the Laplace posterior-mean E[Q]: logq_map = clip(b*s_map - shift + 0.5 b^2 var_post, +-7), with var_post = mean(1/H(k)), H(k) = ps/P(k) + b^2 median(lambda_map_row) — the FFT-diagonal Hessian, so a data-free bin reads logQ->0 (Q=1 homogeneous) and data-rich bins recover Q(s_map). laplace_lognormal_members draws ensemble members s_map + Re ifft(sqrt(1/H)*fft(white)), clipped, deterministic given seed; logq_mean = log(mean(Q_members)).

GP3D MODE: one low-rank 3-D field over all occupied (pixel x z) voxels using the exact (sphere x zeta) GP of darksirens.sky.models (_sphere_z_kernel: chordal-RBF on unit vectors n-hat x RBF in zeta=log1p(z); float64 forced). Inducing nodes (lowrank_inducing_nodes): Fibonacci sphere M_sph=32 crossed with linspace(0, log1p(z_node_hi=3.0), M_z=6) in zeta, ordering i = i_sph*M_z + i_z, M=192, node-for-node identical to the online sky GP. Whitened operator (build_lowrank_operator): K = k(Z,Z) + jitter*I (jitter = 1e-4*amp^2 + 1e-9), L = chol(K), Phi = k(X,Z) L^{-T}, field f = Phi @ xi with xi ~ N(0,I); sum(Phi^2, axis=1) = k(x,Z)K^{-1}k(Z,x) is the per-voxel Nystrom prior variance sigma2_vox used for the mean-one shift, so logQ = b*Phi@xi - 0.5 b^2 sigma2_vox per draw. MAP (poisson_lognormal_gp3d_map) is a single convex GLM in the M whitened latents: J(xi) = 0.5||xi||^2 + sum_v [lam_v - N_obs_v log lam_v], lam_v = base_v exp(b (Phi xi)_v - shift_v), base_v = C_v*dN_exp_v (active mask base_v>0). Newton with Armijo on H = I + b^2 Phi^T diag(lam) Phi; field clipped at |f|<=10 with KKT-projected gradient/Hessian (pinned outward-pressing voxels carry no gradient/curvature); L-BFGS-B fallback; convergence judged on gradient inf-norm relative to gscale = max(1, b*max|N_obs|), tol=1e-8, with bounded-least-squares KKT-multiplier absorption at kink minima. H_chol (chol of MAP Hessian) feeds both laplace_lognormal_gp3d_members (xi_m = xi_map + L_H^{-T} g, Cov = H^{-1}, full cross-pixel/z correlation, deterministic given seed) and the output table. eval_logq_gp3d, the table the GW likelihood consumes: deterministic posterior mean logQ = b*f_MAP - 0.5 b^2 (prior_var - post_var), post_var = phi H^{-1} phi^T, evaluated chunked over pixels directly on the package zgrid (no interpolation); data-free voxels have post_var = prior_var so logQ=0 exactly; per-draw mode uses logQ = b*f - 0.5 b^2 prior_var and its member mean reproduces the posterior mean.

HYPERPARAMETERS AND DATA (from the CLI builder). amp = survey.lss_sigma = 1.0; ls_sph = survey.lss_corr_length_ang = 0.2 (chordal); lss_corr_length_mpc = 50.0 (core/types.py defaults). Radial: solved on a uniform comoving-chi grid, ell_grid = 50 Mpc / dchi_uniform. GP3D: ls_z = 50 Mpc * dzeta/dchi at count-weighted z_ref = sum(z*N)/sum(N), i.e. ls_z = L_mpc / ((1+z_ref) dchi/dz|z_ref); coarse solve z-grid (gp3d_nz_solve nodes, field low-rank in z). bias = survey.b_miss. The fit conditions on: per-pixel KDE-binned observed counts N_obs; expected observed counts C * dN_exp where dN_exp = n0 apix dV_c/dz (1+z)^delta bin-integrated in z between chi-bin edges (a documented Jacobian fix: point-evaluation missed dz/dchi ~ c/H and railed tables at the -7 clip), and C is the expectation-weighted bin average of the kernel-ratio completeness clip(dN_obs_kde/dN_exp_smooth, 0, 1) — the same matched-kernel C the completion machinery uses. Only occupied pixels are fit; empty pixels get logQ=0.

DOCUMENTED CAVEATS. (1) Radial mode has no angular coupling between lines of sight (gp3d lifts this). (2) C and Q come from the SAME observed counts, so Q is the sub-smoothing radial residual, not separately identifiable completeness; the model assumes missing galaxies trace observed clustering (not validatable from data alone). (3) Built at fixed fiducial cosmology/survey parameters; the likelihood consumes the deterministic/posterior-mean Q, not the fully marginalized ensemble. (4) The Laplace machinery is explicitly "not a full BORG sampler". (5) HDF5 I/O is fail-closed (non-finite tables never written/loaded; atomic rename; realization_set_id/member sha256 provenance; loud warnings for unconverged or legacy-maxfun-capped files).
code.codeLik:
The dark-siren prior is the Gray/Gair in-out density decomposition, assembled once per parameter proposal in `prepare_redshift_prior_state` (prior.py) and evaluated per PE/injection sample by `_eval_dark_scalar`:

p(z|pix) = [N_obs(pix)·p_cat(z|pix) + dN_miss(z|pix)] / Z.

Observed branch. `catalog_kernel_state` builds per-galaxy truncated-Gaussian kernels (broadened by sampled sigma_kde); p_cat is the per-pixel unit-normalized weighted KDE. Its amplitude is the real-galaxy row count N_obs, depth-scaled by exp(log_depth_mass) when survey.z_depth truncates the kernels (avoids double counting above-depth galaxies). Writing N_obs·p_cat sets catalog:missing odds to count odds while the within-catalog shape follows weights. Marked-host models replace N_obs with the h(m|eta)-weighted mass and multiply the missing branch by mu_miss(z|eta)=E_obs[h|z].

Missing branch (completion.py). dN_exp(z) = n0·apix·dV_c/dz·(1+z)^delta with sampled {log10 n0, delta}. Differential completeness is the matched-kernel ratio C(z|pix) = clip(dN_obs_s/dN_exp_s, 0, 1), both sides smoothed by the same operator; dN_obs_s comes from `_row_C`, which indexes the `dN_obs_kde` cache directly by row. Then dN_miss = (1−C)·dN_exp·lss, where the rate factor lss is exactly one of two mutually exclusive things: (a) a precomputed Q_LSS table (`lss_completion_logq`/`_q`), which REPLACES (b) the legacy local-overdensity factor max(1 + alpha_miss·b_miss·delta_g(pix,z), 0) with sampled b_miss. `completion_curves` picks the Q path whenever a table (or ensemble posterior mean) resolves; `field_global_log_Z` hard-errors if both field_lss_q and field_delta_g are present. `lss_completion_indexing` (int enum 0=auto/1=compact/2=global) is decoded EAGERLY in the likelihood factory, pre-jit, delivering row-aligned tables; inside the trace `_resolve_lss_completion_row_tables` only consumes them. Under z_depth, beyond the depth C:=0 and lss:=1, so dN_miss=dN_exp (hosts are missing, not nonexistent); N_miss = ∫dN_miss dz over the full grid.

Q ensembles. With `lss_completion_*_members` the state (`DarkSirenEnsemblePriorState`) keeps scalar posterior-mean-Q fields plus a member-independent base_miss=(1−C)·dN_exp and compact per-member log_Z_members; member m's density is reconstructed on the fly as base_miss·Q_eff_m at the two zgrid bracket nodes (`eval_dark_member_completion`), never storing the (M,N_rows,N_grid) cube. Under lss_marginalize, core.py factors the member-independent work (`eval_dark_obs_bracket`: KDE + bracket) once and vmaps only the completion over members.

Sky weighting. "conditional" (legacy): Z = Z[pix] = N_obs(pix)+N_miss(pix); every pixel integrates to unit mass, relative angular host density is discarded (radial-only estimand). "field" (CLI default): the numerator is unchanged but the normalizer is the survey-global Z = Σ_pix[N_obs+N_miss] (`field_global_log_Z`, built from field_dN_obs_s / field_n_empty / field_N_obs_total, with the SAME budget modulation via field_lss_q or field_delta_g rows and depth-scaled observed totals), so pixels are weighted by their host content and, at K≥2, the mixture weight measures the host fraction. Field mode requires matching field_* inputs for any active modulation (Q table, ensemble, real delta_g, marks, depth), or numerator and normalizer would carry different missing budgets. dark_sirens_complete field mode uses the theta-independent Z=Σ N_obs.

Likelihood coupling (core.py). The SAME catalog-completed prior state feeds both the per-event PE term and the selection integral (`selection_prior_model` pins dark models to themselves — the self-calibrating estimator; the sampled survey block {log10n0, delta, b_miss, sigma_kde}, Q_LSS and eta must enter mu(Lambda,Theta) or the prior can reshape with no detectability penalty). Per sample the evaluator gathers only dN_miss[pix, idx:idx+2] and log_Nobs[pix], logaddexp's, and subtracts log_Z[pix] or log_Z_global.

What the inference is actually sensitive to. Not the total galaxy density. In conditional mode the per-pixel prior depends only on the RATIO of the missing density to the total, i.e. the odds N_obs(pix):dN_miss(z|pix) and the z-shape of dN_miss — any common rescaling of both branches cancels in Z[pix]. n0 enters only through C(z;n0) (the completeness ratio) and the amplitude of dN_miss relative to the fixed observed count, hence its weak identification. At K=1 field mode, log_Z_global cancels between PE and selection, so the net effect is just restoring relative angular weighting (angular distribution of N_obs+N_miss); log10n0's dedicated global-Z channel vanishes. Only at K≥2 field do the absolute per-catalog totals Z_k matter (non-cancelling mixture weights = host fractions). A redesign's true target is therefore dN_miss(z|pix) — its redshift shape and its amplitude relative to N_obs per pixel (plus, in field mode, its angular distribution) — not the absolute total density.

literature.litPipes:
DARK SIREN CATALOG-INCOMPLETENESS TREATMENTS — DIGEST

Common framing. All pipelines write the redshift/host prior as a mixture: p(z, Omega | catalog) = P_complete(z, Omega) * p_cat + [1 - P_complete] * p_miss, i.e. they must specify (a) "how much is missing" — a completeness fraction P(z, Omega), and (b) "where the missing galaxies go" — the spatial/redshift distribution assumed for uncataloged hosts. The pipelines differ mainly in the angular resolution of (a) and the physical realism of (b).

1) gwcosmo v1 (Gray et al. 2020, arXiv:1908.06050). Sky-averaged treatment. "How much": a single apparent-magnitude threshold mth for the whole catalog (median apparent magnitude of the sample); the probability the host is in the catalog, p(G|z, H0), is computed by integrating an assumed Schechter luminosity function above/below the luminosity corresponding to mth at each z. "Where": missing galaxies are assumed uniform in comoving volume (homogeneous completion), optionally luminosity-weighted via the same Schechter function. No angular dependence; the split is purely LF-based and global. Applied to GW170817 without counterpart and O2 events (Gray et al. and the LVK O2/O3 H0 papers, e.g. arXiv:1908.06060).

2) gwcosmo pixelated (Gray et al. 2022, arXiv:2111.04629). Same LF machinery, but the sky is divided into HEALPix pixels and each pixel gets its own mth (median apparent magnitude of galaxies in that pixel), making completeness directionally dependent — important for GLADE, whose depth varies strongly across the sky (e.g. 2MASS vs SDSS footprints, Galactic plane). "Where" is unchanged: within each pixel the out-of-catalog part is homogeneous-in-comoving-volume beyond what the LF says is observed. So: per-pixel magnitude limits for the amount; homogeneous + Schechter weighting for the placement.

3) gwcosmo LOS redshift prior (Gray et al. 2023, arXiv:2308.02281). Reformulates the pixelated method as a precomputed line-of-sight redshift prior p(z|Omega): along each pixel, the prior is the sum of an "in-catalogue" part (delta-like/Gaussian-smoothed contributions from cataloged galaxies with luminosity or uniform weighting) and an analytic "out-of-catalogue" part built from the Schechter function below the per-pixel mth, normalized so the two parts sum consistently. This makes the amount/placement split explicit and enables joint cosmology + population inference; the missing part is still homogeneous in angle within a pixel and LF-distributed in z. Used in the GWTC-3 cosmology analysis (LVK, arXiv:2111.03604).

4) DarkSirensStat (Finke et al. 2021, arXiv:2101.12660). The most explicit about the placement question. "How much": completeness P_complete(z, Omega) estimated empirically — either "mask completeness" (angular masks with completeness vs z per region) or "cone completeness" — by comparing the observed luminosity (or number) density in GLADE to the expected mean density, rather than from an mth + LF alone. "Where": two limiting schemes and an interpolation. Homogeneous completion places missing galaxies uniformly (they contribute where the catalog is empty); multiplicative completion assumes missing galaxies trace the cataloged ones (upweights existing structure, i.e. clustering-informed placement). DarkSirensStat interpolates between them: multiplicative where the catalog is fairly complete (missing galaxies likely trace observed overdensities), homogeneous where it is largely incomplete. This is the first mainstream pipeline to treat "where the missing galaxies go" as a modeling choice with clustering information, not just a homogeneous default.

5) ICAROGW 2.0 (Mastrogiovanni et al. 2023, arXiv:2305.17973; method paper arXiv:2103.14663). Implements essentially the gwcosmo-style LF completion within a hierarchical population framework: GLADE+ K-band (or bs) galaxies, HEALPix pixelization, per-pixel mth defined as the median apparent magnitude of galaxies in the pixel (galaxies fainter than mth are cut for self-consistency — the same cut defines both the retained catalog and the completeness model). Completeness fraction from Schechter-function integration above/below mth; out-of-catalog term homogeneous in comoving volume with optional luminosity weighting (L^alpha or Schechter-weighted hosts). Used for GWTC-3 modified-GW-propagation analyses (arXiv:2309.03833). No clustering-informed completion.

6) CHIMERA (Borghi et al. 2023, arXiv:2312.05302). Original release assumed complete (spectroscopic or photometric) catalogs, focusing on the jointly hierarchical cosmology+population likelihood with kernel-density LOS redshift priors per pixel. Incompleteness was added in the follow-up "Echoes from the dark" (Tagliaferri, Borghi et al. 2025, arXiv:2509.18243), which implements a self-consistent homogeneous completion in the public pipeline: completeness fraction (e.g. from magnitude/mass cuts applied to simulated catalogs) plus a homogeneous out-of-catalog term, tested against catalogs of varying completeness and host-weighting (stellar-mass) schemes on O5-like mocks. Placement is homogeneous; the emphasis is on self-consistency between the simulated cut and the correction, and on how mass-weighting interacts with incompleteness.

7) GLADE/GLADE+ mth practice (Dalya et al. 2022, arXiv:2110.06184). GLADE+ itself quantifies completeness globally by comparing integrated B-band luminosity to the mean (complete to ~44 Mpc in cumulative B luminosity; contains most K-band luminosity to >~100 Mpc), but has no single survey mth — it is a heterogeneous compilation. Pipelines therefore impose an effective mth themselves: per-HEALPix-pixel median apparent magnitude (gwcosmo 2022/2023, ICAROGW), discarding galaxies fainter than it, so the LF-based completeness model matches the retained sample. Known caveats: the median-mth choice throws away real galaxies and is only an approximation to the true selection function; recent work proposes more robust per-pixel mth estimation (arXiv:2502.14164) and quantifies residual sensitivity to completeness modeling (arXiv:2511.04786, arXiv:2511.12334).

Summary table (amount / placement): gwcosmo 2020: global mth + Schechter / homogeneous. gwcosmo 2022–23: per-pixel mth + Schechter / homogeneous within pixel. DarkSirensStat: empirical density-based P(z,Omega) with masks / interpolated multiplicative (clustering-informed) <-> homogeneous. ICAROGW: per-pixel median mth + Schechter / homogeneous, luminosity-weighted hosts. CHIMERA: assumed complete originally; homogeneous completion with self-consistent cuts since arXiv:2509.18243. None yet uses a full clustering/large-scale-structure reconstruction for the missing component; DarkSirensStat's multiplicative scheme is the closest.
literature.litLSS:
LSS/CLUSTERING-INFORMED CATALOG COMPLETION FOR DARK-SIREN REDSHIFT PRIORS — RESEARCH DIGEST

1. Baseline: homogeneous vs. clustering-informed completion
Standard dark-siren pipelines (gwcosmo, DarkSirensStat, e.g. Finke et al., arXiv:2101.12660) complete magnitude-limited catalogs either "homogeneously" (missing galaxies uniform in comoving volume) or "multiplicatively" (out-of-catalog counts scaled proportionally to in-catalog counts). Neither is physical: homogeneous filling erases structure below the magnitude limit; multiplicative completion overestimates structure amplitude at low completeness. The methods below are the published attempts to put actual clustering information into the completion or into the redshift prior itself.

2. Methods that put clustering into the completion step

- Dalang & Baker, "The clustering of dark sirens' invisible host galaxies" (arXiv:2310.08991, JCAP 2024): first systematic treatment of completion as a statistical inference of the out-of-catalog galaxy field. Proposes a "variance completion" estimator that uses knowledge of the two-point statistics of large-scale structure (effectively a conditional expectation of the missing counts given the observed counts) to interpolate between homogeneous and multiplicative limits. Shows it can drastically outperform both when the catalog preserves the true structure well enough.

- Dalang, Fiorini & Baker, "Large scale structure prior knowledge in the dark siren method" (arXiv:2410.03275): the practical implementation paper. Casts variance completion as a ratio that slots directly into existing line-of-sight redshift-prior computations, and demonstrates it on GLADE+ within gwcosmo. This is the most directly reusable clustering-informed line-of-sight prior in the gwcosmo ecosystem.

- Leyde, Baker & Enzi, "Cosmic Cartography" (arXiv:2409.20531, JCAP 2024): fully Bayesian, BORG-style field-level reconstruction applied to an incomplete magnitude-limited catalog. Models the galaxy counts per voxel with a (lognormal-type) density field prior with cosmological power spectrum plus galaxy bias, infers the posterior on the true number counts per voxel marginalized over cosmology and bias, and simultaneously infers the absolute-magnitude distribution (which the catalog alone does not give). Quantified per-voxel uncertainties make it the most complete published "clustering in the completion" scheme; explicitly aimed at dark-siren redshift priors.

- Mukherjee, Lavaux, Bouchet, Jasche, Wandelt, Nissanke, Leclercq & Hotokezaka (arXiv:1909.08627, A&A 646, A65): BORG proper applied to 2M++ (Bayesian forward-model reconstruction with a particle-mesh solver) to obtain the density and peculiar-velocity field around GW170817 for the velocity correction to H0. This is BORG applied to an incomplete magnitude-limited survey in a GW-cosmology context, though used for velocity debiasing rather than host redshift priors per se; it is the template for "Bayesian density reconstruction feeding a siren analysis."

- Related empirical support: bright-galaxy-subset analyses (e.g. arXiv:2505.11268; also arXiv:2511.04786, "How Low Can You Go") show that the constraining power of severely incomplete catalogs survives largely because faint (missing) galaxies cluster around the bright ones — i.e., clustering-informed completion is capturing real information that homogeneous filling throws away.

3. Cross-correlation methods (clustering used instead of per-galaxy completion)
These sidestep completion: the redshift information comes from the spatial cross-correlation of GW source positions with the (biased) galaxy field, so incompleteness only rescales the bias rather than corrupting a per-line-of-sight prior.

- Oguri (arXiv:1603.02356, PRD 93, 083511, 2016): foundational proposal — cross-correlate GW sources binned in luminosity distance with photometric galaxies binned in redshift; the correct distance–redshift mapping maximizes the signal; includes lensing modulation.
- Mukherjee, Wandelt, Nissanke & Silvestri (arXiv:2007.02943): forecast formalism for precision cosmology with redshift-unknown GW sources via 3D cross-correlation, exploiting the galaxy bias.
- Diaz & Mukherjee (arXiv:2107.12787, MNRAS 511, 2782, 2022): mapping the expansion history with LVK dark sirens in synergy with DESI/SPHEREx.
- Mukherjee, Krolewski, Wandelt & Silk (arXiv:2203.03643, ApJ 2024): first data application — GWTC-3 dark sirens cross-correlated with 2MPZ and WISE-SuperCOSMOS photometric surveys, H0 ≈ 75.4 (median, wide errors).
- Ghosh, More, Bera & Bose (arXiv:2312.16305): Bayesian framework for cross-correlating individual GW events with galaxies for H0 — a bridge between per-event statistical-host methods and ensemble cross-correlation. Related: Bera, Rana, More & Bose (arXiv:2007.04271, ApJ 902, 79) showed the information content of statistical-host H0 inference is controlled by host clustering, motivating all of the above.
- Vijaykumar, Saketh, Kumar, Ajith & Roy Choudhury (arXiv:2005.01111, PRD 108, 103017): BBH auto-correlation as an LSS probe (bias of the BBH population with XG detectors) — establishes GW sources as clustered tracers, the physical basis of the cross-correlation redshift priors.
- Recent extensions: flux-limited catalog cross-correlation H0 (arXiv:2510.22187); GW×galaxy cross-correlation forecasts for XG interferometers × Euclid (arXiv:2504.10482); unified harmonic framework for dark sirens (arXiv:2603.13053); standard-ruler variant (arXiv:2412.00202).

4. Photometric angular-clustering completeness
No dedicated widely-cited paper does "completeness estimation from angular clustering of a photometric survey" for dark sirens specifically; the closest published work is the flux-limited-catalog cross-correlation treatment (arXiv:2510.22187) and the harmonic-space framework (arXiv:2603.13053), which absorb angular selection/completeness into the tracer bias and selection function rather than estimating it from clustering. This appears to be an open niche.

5. Bottom line
Published methods that genuinely put clustering information INTO the completion (not homogeneous filling): Dalang & Baker 2310.08991 and Dalang, Fiorini & Baker 2410.03275 (variance completion, two-point statistics, gwcosmo-ready); Leyde, Baker & Enzi 2409.20531 (Bayesian field-level lognormal/BORG-style reconstruction with magnitude-function inference); and Mukherjee et al. 1909.08627 (true BORG reconstruction of 2M++, velocity correction). The cross-correlation line (Oguri 1603.02356; Mukherjee et al. 2007.02943, 2203.03643; Diaz & Mukherjee 2107.12787; Ghosh et al. 2312.16305) uses clustering as the redshift information itself, bypassing explicit completion.

STATISTICAL FOUNDATIONS DIGEST: THINNED POISSON DECOMPOSITION INTO SELECTION x DENSITY

1. Identifiability of selection vs. density (thinning/mark degeneracy)
An inhomogeneous Poisson process with intensity lambda(x) = phi(x) * n(x) (selection times density) is observationally equivalent to any factorization phi'(x) * n'(x) with the same product: the likelihood depends only on lambda. The degeneracy is broken only by external structure — a parametric/known form for phi (e.g., flux-limit completeness measured from injections), differing smoothness/lengthscale priors on the two fields, or multiplicity of realizations sharing one factor. The statistics literature formalizes this in "preferential sampling": Diggle, Menezes & Su (JRSS-C 59, 191, 2010) model observation locations as a log-Gaussian Cox process (LGCP) whose intensity depends on the latent field, and show that ignoring the coupling biases inference, while at least one parameter of the joint model is inherently weakly identified (see also Dinsdale & Salibian-Barrera, "Methods for preferential sampling in geostatistics," JRSS-C 68, 181, 2019; and "On ignorability of preferential sampling," arXiv:2511.03158). Practical upshot: never try to learn a free selection surface and a free density field from one catalog; fix or strongly constrain one factor.

2. Poisson-lognormal Cox inference
The canonical model is the LGCP of Møller, Syversveen & Waagepetersen (Scand. J. Stat. 25, 451, 1998): Lambda(u) = exp[Z(u)] with Z Gaussian; all moment properties follow from lognormal formulas. In cosmology the same Poisson-lognormal likelihood underlies BORG-type field-level reconstruction (Jasche & Wandelt, MNRAS 407, 29, 2010 "Fast Hamiltonian sampling for large-scale structure inference"; MNRAS 409, 355, 2010), sampled exactly with HMC over ~10^7 latent amplitudes — the "gold standard" alternative to approximate methods. Kitaura et al. (arXiv:0911.1407) give the Poisson-lognormal filter for recovering nonlinear density from galaxy counts with completeness weights.

3. Jensen-type biases when exponentiating lognormal fields
If delta_g = exp(Z) with Z ~ N(mu, sigma^2), then E[exp(Z)] = exp(mu + sigma^2/2) != exp(E[Z]). Any pipeline that (a) fits a Gaussian log-density and then exponentiates the posterior mean, or (b) builds completeness weights from exp of a smoothed/approximated log-field, incurs a multiplicative bias exp(sigma^2/2) that is spatially varying because the conditional variance sigma^2(x) grows where data are sparse — i.e., exactly where completeness corrections matter most. The mean-intensity formula in Møller et al. (1998) is the standard reference; the same issue appears as "inverse-weighting overestimates density at low completeness" in LSS reconstruction (Kitaura et al. 2009, arXiv:0906.3978). The fix is to propagate the full lognormal posterior (or at least the sigma^2/2 correction), not plug in point estimates.

4. Laplace-approximation variance underestimation in latent Gaussian Cox models
A single Gaussian/Laplace approximation at the posterior mode of a Poisson log-likelihood underestimates variance and misses skewness because the log-Poisson likelihood is asymmetric; this is documented in comparative studies: Taylor & Diggle, "INLA or MCMC? A tutorial and comparative evaluation for spatial prediction in log-Gaussian Cox processes" (arXiv:1202.1738, J. Stat. Comput. Sim. 2014), and Teng, Nathoo & Johnson, "Bayesian computation for LGCPs: a comparative analysis" (J. Stat. Comput. Sim. 2017, PMID 29200537). Variational/Laplace schemes tend to be overconfident in the latent field; MALA/HMC (Brix & Møller) is the exact benchmark.

5. Standard fixes: INLA and marginal-likelihood hyperparameter learning
INLA (Rue, Martino & Chopin, JRSS-B 71, 319, 2009) nests Laplace approximations: it computes the approximate marginal posterior of hyperparameters (lengthscale, variance) via the Laplace-approximated marginal likelihood, numerically integrates over that low-dimensional space, and applies skewness-corrected (simplified Laplace) marginals for the latent field — repairing both the fixed-hyperparameter overconfidence and much of the Gaussian-approximation skew error. For LGCPs specifically, Simpson, Illian, Lindgren, Sørbye & Rue, "Going off grid" (Biometrika 103, 49, 2016; arXiv:1111.0641) attack the point-process likelihood directly with a continuously specified SPDE/GMRF field, achieving high-order convergence versus first-order for counting-cell discretizations; implemented in R-INLA (see also the SPDE gitbook ch. 4, and the lightning LGCP application arXiv:2111.15670). Key principle: hyperparameters (especially lengthscales) should be learned by (approximate) marginal likelihood, not fixed a priori, since the Jensen and variance biases above are lengthscale-dependent.

6. Low-rank/inducing-point GPs and resolution limits
Titsias (AISTATS 2009) variational inducing points give O(NM^2) inference; Burt, Rasmussen & van der Wilk (ICML 2019, arXiv:1903.03571; JMLR 2020, arXiv:2008.00323) prove KL-divergence bounds showing the required M scales with domain size over kernel lengthscale (M ~ O(log^D N) for SE kernels with Gaussian inputs); when the true lengthscale is much smaller than inducing-node spacing, the variational posterior collapses toward the prior mean/variance — a hard resolution floor, not a soft bias (see also "Actually Sparse Variational GPs," Cunningham et al., AISTATS 2023, which motivates B-spline bases and very large M for short lengthscales). For sphere x radial domains: Dutordoir, Durrande & Hensman, "Sparse GPs with Spherical Harmonic Features" (ICML 2020, arXiv:2006.16649; revisited arXiv:2303.15948) diagonalize zonal kernels via Mercer/spherical harmonics — inducing "points" become harmonic features with a clean bandlimit interpretation (resolution limit = max degree l), avoiding node-spacing pathologies on the sky; combine with a 1D radial basis (SPDE or Fourier features, cf. arXiv:2308.14142) in a Kronecker structure.

Sources: arXiv:1111.0641, arXiv:1202.1738, arXiv:1903.03571, arXiv:2008.00323, arXiv:2006.16649, arXiv:2303.15948, arXiv:0911.2496, arXiv:0911.1407, arXiv:0906.3978, arXiv:2511.03158, arXiv:2111.15670, arXiv:2308.14142, Rue et al. 2009 (doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2008.00700.x), Diggle et al. 2010 (doi:10.1111/j.1467-9876.2009.00701.x), Møller et al. 1998 (doi:10.1111/1467-9469.00115), Teng et al. 2017 (PMID 29200537), Titsias AISTATS 2009 (proceedings.mlr.press/v5/titsias09a), Cunningham et al. AISTATS 2023 (proceedings.mlr.press/v206/cunningham23a).

DIGEST: Completeness estimation practice in galaxy surveys

1. Classical LF-based completeness (V/Vmax lineage)
The traditional approach is luminosity-function-based: Schmidt's V/Vmax and its descendants estimate completeness by asking what fraction of a fiducial LF a flux-limited sample can see, never by comparing observed counts to a local expectation. GLADE+ (arXiv:2110.06184) is the canonical example in the dark-siren context: completeness is quantified (i) by comparing integrated B-band luminosity of catalog galaxies within distance shells to the value expected from a reference Schechter function, and (ii) by comparing the observed luminosity distribution per shell to the Schechter form. Crucially these are averages over full shells (or the whole extragalactic sky), so large-scale structure averages out; GLADE+ is ~complete to ~130 Mpc by these measures. The "Luminosity of the Darkness" paper (arXiv:2505.13568) shows the sensitivity of dark-siren H0 to the assumed Schechter model and its redshift evolution.

2. Per-pixel depth maps and injection-based completeness
Modern imaging surveys estimate per-healpix-pixel completeness from *observing conditions or injections, explicitly not from galaxy counts*:
- DES "survey property" (SP) maps: depth, seeing, airmass, exposure count, extinction, stellar density per healpix pixel (DES Y3 lens-sample systematics, arXiv:2105.13540).
- Balrog synthetic-source injection: DES Y3 "Measuring the Survey Transfer Function with Balrog" (arXiv:2012.12825) and DES Y6 full-footprint SSI with 146M injections over 5000 deg2 (arXiv:2501.05683). Detection probability vs true magnitude and position gives completeness that is by construction independent of the real galaxy density field.
- Obiwan for the Legacy Surveys/DESI: eBOSS ELG application (arXiv:2007.08992) and DESI LRG forward modeling with 15M simulated galaxies (arXiv:2405.16299); recovers depth-driven density trends and shows faint galaxies dominate them.
LSST plans the same architecture (SP maps + injections, e.g. metadetect/SSI heritage from DES).

3. Separating angular selection from true clustering
When counts must be corrected, surveys regress observed density against *external templates* of observing conditions, never against the counts themselves: Ross et al. BOSS systematics (arXiv:1203.6499), DES Y1 (arXiv:1708.01536), DES Y3 (arXiv:2105.13540), DESI ELG neural-net weights via SYSNET (arXiv:2411.12024), mode projection (Elsner et al., arXiv:1509.08933). The standard guidance against absorbing clustering is explicit and quantitative:
- Even template regression removes true power by chance correlation ("overcorrection"/"false correction bias"); Rezaie et al. (arXiv:1907.11355) show nonlinear methods overfit and bias fNL-like scales, calibrating the max number of templates on contaminated mocks.
- Weaverdyck & Huterer (arXiv:2007.14499) is the systematic comparison: all count-based corrections must be debiased using mocks with no contamination, and template maps must be signal-independent.
- DES/DESI validate weights by applying them to uncontaminated mocks and measuring how much genuine clustering they delete (arXiv:2105.13540, arXiv:2411.12024).
The motivation for Balrog/Obiwan is precisely that injection-based transfer functions cannot absorb clustering because they never look at the real source density.

4. Completeness vs purity for photo-z/candidate catalogs
Quasar/photo-z catalogs report a completeness-purity decomposition (fraction of true objects recovered vs contamination of the selected sample): Quaia (Storey-Fisher et al., arXiv:2306.17749) publishes an all-sky per-pixel selection function built by fitting the observed quasar density with a Gaussian process on *physically motivated templates only* (SFD dust, Gaia stellar density, Magellanic Cloud maps, Gaia/unWISE scanning laws) — templates cap how much true clustering the fit can absorb, though residual absorption at template-correlated scales is acknowledged in follow-up clustering papers (e.g. arXiv:2306.17748). DESI LS photo-z target-selection papers (e.g. LRG/QSO validation, arXiv:2208.08511) quote completeness/purity against spectroscopic truth samples, again not from counts.

5. KEY QUESTION: does anyone estimate per-pixel completeness from the observed counts themselves?
Yes — but in the dark-siren literature, not the surveys. Finke et al. (DarkSirensStat, arXiv:2101.12660) define "cone completeness" and "mask completeness": per-direction completeness computed by comparing observed galaxy number (or luminosity) in a pixel/cone to the expected homogeneous density n̄gal. They explicitly flag the clustering-absorption problem: "If S is chosen too small, completing the catalog is equivalent to smoothing out true structures... if we artificially deem that void region as incomplete [we erase the void's cosmological information]"; their mitigation is a coarse-graining compromise (regions large enough to be statistically fair samples) plus interpolation. gwcosmo (Gray et al.; GWTC-3 cosmology arXiv:2111.03604; gwcosmo 2.0 arXiv:2308.02281) instead does per-pixel completeness via a limiting apparent magnitude m_thr per healpix pixel (median magnitude, or robustly estimated in arXiv:2502.14164) combined with a Schechter LF — counts enter only through the magnitude *distribution*, not the number density, so local over/underdensities do not masquerade as completeness variations. Recent work (arXiv:2511.04786) stress-tests incompleteness effects on dark-siren cosmology.

Bottom line: imaging surveys uniformly avoid counts-based per-pixel completeness (guidance: template regression debiased on mocks, or better, injections — arXiv:2007.14499, 1907.11355, 2012.12825); the counts-based per-pixel construction exists only in dark-siren catalog completion (arXiv:2101.12660), where its clustering-absorption pathology is acknowledged and handled by coarse-graining, while gwcosmo's magnitude-threshold+LF method (arXiv:2308.02281, 2502.14164) is the clustering-safe alternative.

PROPOSAL: SKY-AGGREGATE C + FULL-OVERDENSITY Q

1. Estimator math

Replace per-pixel C with one aggregate radial curve. Let F be the survey footprint (N_pix HEALPix pixels, occupied AND empty). Numerator: the all-galaxy smoothed KDE (sum of the existing cached rows, or one pass over all z_i):

  dN_obs_s,tot(z) = Σ_{p∈F} dN_obs_s(z|p) = Σ_{i, real} N(z; z_i, σ)/M(z_i)

Denominator: the isotropic expectation times pixel count, smoothed by the SAME operator S:

  C̄(z) = clip( dN_obs_s,tot(z) / [ N_pix · (S dN_exp)(z) ], 0, 1 ),  dN_exp = n0·apix·dV_c/dz·(1+z)^δ

This is exactly the aggregate the closure experiment validated to 0.3%: density fluctuations average out over the footprint (Σ_p δ_p ≈ 0), so C̄ estimates only the selection φ(z). All angular structure moves to Q, whose target becomes the FULL missing-tracer overdensity, not the sub-smoothing residual:

  Q_target(p,z) = 1 + δ_miss(p,z) ≈ dN_obs_s(z|p) / [ C̄(z)·(S dN_exp)(z) ]  (shrunk toward 1 where data are sparse)

  dN_miss(z|p) = (1 − C̄(z)) · dN_exp(z) · Q(p,z),  with per-z mean-one enforcement Q̃(p,z) = Q(p,z)·N_pix/Σ_{p'∈F} Q(p',z)

The renormalization is the how-much/where contract: C̄ alone fixes Σ_p dN_miss = N_pix(1−C̄)dN_exp; Q only redistributes it.

2. Module changes

completion.py: add C_mode enum ("per_pixel" legacy default, "aggregate") in core/types.py. In _precompute_grids compute C̄ once per proposal (one curve; cheaper than N_rows×N_grid _row_C — reuse the summed field_dN_obs_s rows, f64 accumulation). _row_C becomes a broadcast in aggregate mode; _assemble_curves and field_global_log_Z unchanged in form (C row is constant across pixels; V(z) simplifies to (1−C̄)ΣQ_p). z_depth logic unchanged (C̄:=0, Q:=1 beyond depth). Legacy δ_g path: change compute_lss_overdensity's mean to run over ALL footprint pixels (not occupied only) and give empty pixels δ_g from smoothed neighbors rather than 0, so voids read δ_g<0 instead of homogeneous.

lognormal_completion.py: swap the conditioning base from base_v = C(p)·dN_exp_v to base_v = C̄_v·dN_exp_v (bin-averaged with the existing Jacobian treatment), and INCLUDE EMPTY PIXELS in the fit with N_obs=0 — zero counts against a nonzero base is exactly the void information now missing ("deep voids fitted at Q~1"). Keep the posterior-mean E[Q] Laplace output and mean-one shift; add the per-z mean-one renormalization at table-write time (kills the radial mode's ~55% Jensen inflation of the budget by construction — noise can no longer change the total, only the placement).

CLI (build_lognormal_completion.py): expose lss_corr_length_mpc, lss_sigma, gp3d z-node count/range, and M_sph as flags (currently only container defaults; the shipped 50 Mpc → ls_z ~30× below the 6-node spacing is unfixable from the CLI). Enforce node spacing ≤ ls_z at build time (hard error, not warning).

Provenance/backward compat: Q tables record c_mode in HDF5 attrs; completion_curves fail-closed if a per-pixel-base table is consumed in aggregate mode or vice versa (the two targets differ by the whole clustering signal — mixing double-counts or drops it). Legacy per-pixel path untouched; aggregate is opt-in per survey config. test_cache_row_indexing unaffected (cache still row-indexed; aggregate just sums it).

3. Identifiability

The thinning degeneracy λ = φ·n is broken by structure, not data: (a) the aggregate assumption — selection isotropic, density mean-one over the footprint — makes C̄ estimate φ alone; (b) at low z the shell contains few correlation volumes (sample-variance floor Var[C̄]/C̄² ~ σ²_δ·V_corr/V_shell), but there C̄≈1, so the clip at 1 plus an optional isotonic (monotone non-increasing) constraint on C̄(z) absorbs it at second order; (c) the magnitude-limit physics (Schechter integral above m_th → erf-like roll-off) is available as a parametric prior mean for C̄, and the luminosity function is the principled cross-check — but the closure evidence says the data-driven aggregate already closes to 0.3%, so keep it primary. For genuinely anisotropic depth (GLADE: 2MASS vs SDSS, Galactic plane) the isotropy assumption fails; the sanctioned "low-order" escape is stratification: K coarse depth regions (e.g. m_th quantile masks), one C̄_k(z) each — selection ~constant within a stratum, density still averages out. Q must never carry secular depth gradients; that is the degeneracy re-entering.

4. What this fixes (closure failures)

- Anti-correlation r=−0.43/slope −0.62: root cause was per-pixel C absorbing +δ so (1−C) anti-tracks truth. With C̄ flat across sky, (1−C̄) is pixel-independent and Q carries +δ: correlation flips positive by construction.
- Clipping loss: overdense complete pixels no longer read C>1→clip 1; their excess lives in Q, nothing discarded.
- gp3d slope 0.29→~1: target is now full δ (not residual) AND node spacing fixed via CLI; for the 800 Mpc mock, ls_z resolvable with modest M_z.
- Voids at Q~1: empty pixels enter the fit as zeros.
- Depth-edge spikes: C̄ is a smooth aggregate; the per-pixel C→small noise that inflated (1−C) at the edge disappears.
- Radial Jensen +55%: mean-one-per-z renormalization makes the budget Q-noise-invariant.

5. Failure modes

Anisotropic selection leaking into Q (mitigate: stratified C̄_k; validate no Q–m_th correlation); low-rank resolution floor for real ~10–50 Mpc clustering at M=192 (fails conservative — Q shrinks toward homogeneous, budget still right; scale M_sph/M_z or move to spherical-harmonic features); gp3d Laplace overconfidence (5% coverage) is unchanged by this redesign — flag ensembles as unreliable pending INLA-style hyperparameter marginalization; partial-sky footprints raise the sample-variance floor on C̄; b_miss≠b_obs remains a prior assumption (sampled b_miss still scales logQ).

6. Validation

Rerun experiments/completeness_viz closure end-to-end in aggregate mode with rebuilt Q tables. Acceptance: aggregate C̄ vs generative selection ≤0.5%; per-pixel missing-branch correlation r>0.6 with POSITIVE slope ~1 (vs −0.62); assembled total-density slope ~1 (vs 0.25 homogeneous / 0.77 legacy); dN/dz budget closure ≤1% for all Q modes (radial currently +55%); fitted-vs-truth logQ slope ~1 for gp3d (vs 0.04 shipped); void pixels (true Q~0.2) recovered Q<0.5; no depth-edge spike in dN_miss; member coverage reported but not gating. Regression: legacy per-pixel mode bit-identical.

Key files: /hildafs/projects/phy230014p/magana/src/darksirens-dev/darksirens/redshift/completion.py (_precompute_grids 624-632, _row_C 876-901, _assemble_curves 904-957, δ_g 1753-1826), /hildafs/projects/phy230014p/magana/src/darksirens-dev/darksirens/redshift/lognormal_completion.py (base construction ~line 137 region, occupied-only fit), /hildafs/projects/phy230014p/magana/src/darksirens-dev/darksirens/cli/build_lognormal_completion.py (hyperparameter flags), /hildafs/projects/phy230014p/magana/src/darksirens-dev/darksirens/core/types.py (C_mode, corr-length knobs).

PROPOSAL — ANGLE 2: surgical fixes to the existing C/Q machinery, priority-ordered by closure impact per unit effort.

P0. Promote delta_g at low density (item e, minimal form). Effort: hours. The closure evidence is unambiguous at n0~1e-5 Mpc^-3: legacy lss = max(1 + b_eff*delta_g(p,z), 0) achieves total-density slope 0.77, r=0.68, budget closure 0.6%, logQ slope 1.05, versus gp3d's 0.29 and homogeneous's anti-correlation (r=-0.43). Change: in docs/CLI defaults (darksirens/cli/build_lognormal_completion.py, prior.py model docs), make the delta_g branch the recommended lss for shot-noise-dominated catalogs (n̄*V_kernel ≲ few per smoothing volume); keep Q tables recommended only for dense surveys. No numerics change. Failure modes: multiplicative completion overstates structure where C is very low (DarkSirensStat's known caveat); the max(.,0) rail clips deep voids; b_miss is degenerate with alpha_miss (already exact, harmless since only b_miss is sampled).

P1. Debias the radial-Q missing budget (item b). Effort: ~1 day, builder-only. The 55% Jensen inflation arises because the table is E[Q] = exp(b*s - shift + 0.5 b^2 var_post) (and for members, log mean_m Q_m): the mean-one shift enforces E[Q]=1 under the *prior*, but posterior noise-fitting plus var_post (which is largest exactly where data are sparse — the Cox-process digest's spatially varying exp(sigma^2/2) bias) inflates the weighted sum. Fix by construction, matching the owner's ideal "C = how much, Q = where": after building any table (radial or gp3d), renormalize per z-bin over occupied pixels

  logQ_p(z) <- logQ_p(z) - log[ Σ_p w_p(z) Q_p(z) / Σ_p w_p(z) ],  w_p(z) = (1 - C_p(z)) * dN_exp(z),

so Σ_p dN_miss with Q equals the homogeneous budget identically — Q becomes a pure redistribution field. Apply the same per-member renormalization inside laplace_lognormal_members (each member individually mean-one under w), so the ensemble carries placement uncertainty but zero budget uncertainty (the budget is C's and n0's job; n0 is sampled). Module: lognormal_completion.py (post-processing before HDF5 write; record the removed monopole in provenance). Fixes: 55% inflation → 0 by construction; also removes the E[Q]-vs-exp(E[logQ]) convention split (both conventions now agree after renorm up to per-pixel shape). Failure mode: deletes any true radial monopole per shell — but that monopole is exactly degenerate with n0*g(z)(1+z)^delta and belongs to the sampled budget, so this is intended; if C is biased, w is biased, but only second-order in the normalization.

P2. Tame the depth-edge spike (item d). Effort: small, one function. Cause: with z_depth set (or a sharp survey edge), galaxy kernels in _kde_dndz_obs renormalize on [0, zmax] (mass = ndtr((_ZMAX - zs)/sigma) - ndtr(-zs/sigma), completion.py:236), while dN_exp_smooth = S @ dN_exp integrates over the full grid (_precompute_grids, :624-632). Just below the edge the numerator loses ~Φ((z-z_edge)/σ) of local mass but the denominator does not, so C dips and dN_miss = (1-C)*dN_exp spikes. Fix: when z_depth is a concrete float, truncate the expected side identically:

  dN_exp_smooth = S @ (dN_exp * 1[z <= z_depth]).

Since the numerator at z < z_depth is exactly S applied to the true (edge-truncated) density, a constant-C survey again passes through the ratio exactly at the edge, mirroring the existing z=0 boundary treatment. One-line change in _precompute_grids (and the field-mode recompute at :1293-1395); above z_depth the existing C:=0 branch takes over. Failure modes: only helps when z_depth is explicit; a data-driven roll-off (no z_depth) keeps its softer edge — mitigate by recommending z_depth be set to the survey's nominal depth in closure/production configs.

P3. Expose and learn the radial lengthscale; fix node spacing (item a). Effort: few days, builder/CLI only. Changes in build_lognormal_completion.py + core/types.py: (i) add --lss-corr-length-mpc (currently line 72: "take their container defaults" — no knob) and --lss-sigma; (ii) make inducing nodes resolve the kernel: z_node_hi := zgrid[-1] (not 3.0 — for the zmax=0.5 mock only ~2 of 6 zeta-nodes even touch the data), and

  M_z = clip(ceil(1.5 * log1p(zmax) / ls_z) + 1, 6, 96),  M_sph = clip(ceil(4π * 1.5^2 / ls_sph^2), 32, 512),

per the Burt et al. resolution-floor result (posterior collapses to prior when spacing >> lengthscale — exactly the observed slope 0.04). lowrank_inducing_nodes already takes n_inducing_sphere/n_inducing_z, so this is pure plumbing; cost is offline O(N_vox*M + M^3), fine at M~2000. (iii) Learn ell by Laplace marginal likelihood (INLA-lite): for a small grid {ell_j} (e.g. 5 log-spaced values around the CLI value), reuse the existing MAP+H_chol to compute

  log Z_j ≈ -J(ξ*_j) - Σ log diag(L_H,j) ,

designs.joint:
PROPOSAL — ANGLE 3: joint Poisson-lognormal selection x clustering model

FEASIBILITY CHECK (code read). The mock generator (scripts/mock_dark_sirens/generate_mock_data.py:762-764, 783) draws M ~ N(M0=-21, sigma_M=1), m = M + DM(z), cuts m <= m_lim=24; the closure generator reuses it verbatim and even computes the analytic per-galaxy selection c_true_gal = Phi((m_lim - M0 - DM(z))/sigma_M) (generate_clustered_mock.py:224). But the survey HDF5 written at generate_mock_data.py:1711-1718 drops magnitudes (only TARGET_RA/DEC, Z, ZERR, WEIGHT), and cli/pixelate.py reads only those columns — so magnitudes exist per galaxy in the mock but never reach the pipeline. Real targets: GLADE+ has per-galaxy B/K magnitudes and DESI LS has grz fluxes, so the same column can be populated for real catalogs; the pixelated format already supports optional padded per-galaxy extras (MARK_DATASETS in catalogs/io.py) to template an APP_MAG dataset.

MODEL. Binned counts per (pixel p, z-bin v):

  N_pv ~ Poisson(lambda_pv),  lambda_pv = n0 * DeltaV_pv * C_sel(z_v; theta) * Q_pv
  C_sel(z; theta) = Phi((m_lim - M0 - DM(z)) / sigma_M),  theta = (m_lim, M0, sigma_M)   [Schechter variant: incomplete-gamma]
  Q_pv = exp(b f(p,z_v) - b^2 sigma_f^2(p,z_v)/2),  f = Phi_op @ xi, xi ~ N(0,I)   [existing gp3d whitened low-rank GP]

plus the per-galaxy magnitude likelihood, which is exactly independent of Q (thinning: conditioned on detection at redshift z_i, the magnitude distribution is the truncated LF regardless of local density):

  p(m_i | z_i, theta) = phi(m_i - DM(z_i)) * 1[m_i <= m_lim] / C_sel(z_i; theta)

Joint posterior over (theta, log n0, xi); hyperparameters (sigma_f, ell_ang, ell_z) by Laplace marginal likelihood on a small grid (INLA-style): log Z(hyp) ≈ -J(xi*) - sum log diag(L_H) + const, reusing the H_chol already computed in poisson_lognormal_gp3d_map.

IDENTIFIABILITY. Counts alone give only the product C_sel*Q (thinning degeneracy). Broken three ways: (1) magnitudes pin theta independently of density — the clustering-safe channel the survey literature insists on (mth+LF / injection philosophy); with 277k galaxies theta is pinned to <1%, (2) Q is mean-one with finite learned correlation length, so smooth isotropic radial trends cannot live in Q; (3) monitor the sky-monopole of Q(z) (should be ~1) as a misspecification alarm. Residual n0—Q-monopole degeneracy is killed by the mean-one shift.

TWO-STEP APPROXIMATION (recommended default). Step 1: MLE of theta from Prod_i p(m_i|z_i,theta) (truncated-Gaussian fit; new darksirens/redshift/selection.py), then n0 = N_tot / integral(dV C_sel). Step 2: existing gp3d Poisson-lognormal MAP with base_v := n0 * DeltaV_v * C_sel(z_v; theta_hat) replacing the current base_v = C_kernel * dN_exp, plus the marginal-likelihood hyperparameter loop. Because the magnitude likelihood carries essentially all information about theta and none about Q, this partial-likelihood split loses only (a) theta-uncertainty propagation into Q (negligible at 277k galaxies) and (b) a weak count-shape channel on theta. It captures most of the joint model's benefit at ~zero extra cost over the current builder. The full joint fit (augment xi with 4 scalars, bordered Hessian in the existing Newton) is a validation-grade upgrade, not required.

MODULE CHANGES.
1. generate_mock_data.py + pixelate.py + catalogs/io.py: write/read APP_MAG through survey and pixelated files (padded table like marks).
2. New darksirens/redshift/selection.py: C_sel(z;theta), fit_selection_from_mags.
3. lognormal_completion.py: swap base_v to n0*DeltaV*C_sel; add hyperparameter marginal-likelihood loop; CLI knobs for ell_z / z-node count (currently none — the shipped 50 Mpc default is 30x below node spacing).
4. completion.py/_assemble_curves + field_global_log_Z: missing branch becomes dN_miss(z|p) = (1 - C_sel(z)) * n0 apix dV/dz (1+z)^delta * Q(p,z). The per-pixel kernel-ratio C is demoted to a diagnostic; C is now the isotropic radial budget, Q the spatial field — exactly the owner's ideal split. Observed branch (N_obs*p_cat) untouched.

HOW IT FIXES THE CLOSURE FAILURES. The r=-0.43 anti-correlation exists because per-pixel C absorbs clustering, so (1-C) anti-tracks the true missing density; with isotropic C_sel, dN_miss tracks Q directly (target slope ~1, beating legacy delta_g's 0.77). gp3d's slope 0.29 had two causes, both removed: Q was only the sub-smoothing residual on top of per-pixel C (now it is the whole clustering field) and ell_z was unrepresentable (now learned + resolvable nodes). Deep voids (true Q~0.2) become recoverable because C no longer eats the deficit. The depth-edge spike vanishes: C_sel is smooth and analytic, no KDE-ratio noise, no [0,1] clip activity. The radial-mode 55% Jensen inflation disappears with the cross-pixel gp3d fit and the posterior-mean E[Q] convention. The 5% member coverage is addressed by mixing Laplace members across the hyperparameter grid weighted by Z(hyp) — the dominant overconfidence was fixed-wrong hyperparameters.

FAILURE MODES. (i) LF/selection misspecification on real compilations (GLADE+ has no single m_lim): use per-region m_lim(p) fitted from per-pixel magnitude distributions (gwcosmo-median or arXiv:2502.14164 robust estimator) — still magnitude-derived, still clustering-safe; heterogeneity that is not magnitude-driven leaks into Q's monopole (alarm above). (ii) Photo-z scatter: counts are in z_obs while C_sel is in true z — convolve base_v with the error kernel (the S operator exists). (iii) LF evolution: z-dependent (M0, sigma_M) are identifiable from magnitudes per z-slice but weak at the faint end; freeze evolution or prior-penalize. (iv) Fixed theta_hat vs sampled cosmology in DM(z): C_sel is cheap/analytic, so theta can be sampled inside the GW likelihood (replacing the z50/w phenomenology and entering the selection integral self-consistently), or accepted as fixed-fiducial like current Q tables. (v) Cost: nside16 x 60 bins = 184k voxels, M ~ 10^3 inducing points needed once ell_z is honest; Newton O(V M^2 + M^3) ~ minutes on GPU x ~30 hyperparameter solves — offline, acceptable.

VALIDATION (existing closure experiment, experiments/completeness_viz). The generator already emits app_mag and the exact truth C_sel curve (c_true_gal). (1) Fit theta_hat from mock magnitudes; require C_sel(z; theta_hat) within 1% of c_true_gal and of the current aggregate kernel-ratio C (which already closes to 0.3% — a cross-check, not a target). (2) Rebuild Q with the new base and learned hyperparameters; recompute README metrics: missing-density correlation (target r>0.8, slope 0.9-1.1), fitted-vs-truth logQ slope ~1, dN/dz budget closure <1%, void pixels recovered at Q~0.2, no depth-edge spike, member-band empirical coverage within 10% of nominal. (3) Run the two-step vs the full joint fit on the same mock; agreement of theta posteriors and Q maps within Monte Carlo error certifies the cheap path. (4) Ablation: rerun with magnitudes withheld (counts-only joint fit) to quantify what the magnitude channel buys — this is the direct measurement of the thinning degeneracy.

result.novelty:
GENUINELY NOVEL

1. The end-to-end joint likelihood integration. No published pipeline samples a clustering-informed completion field's hyperparameters (n0, delta, b_miss, sigma_kde) jointly with cosmology+population while forcing the identical completed prior through both the per-event term and the selection integral (the self-calibrating pinning in core.py). gwcosmo/ICAROGW precompute a fixed LOS prior; Leyde et al. (2409.20531) reconstruct the field but stop short of a jointly-sampled GW likelihood. The cube-free member marginalization (base_miss x Q_eff_m reconstructed at bracket nodes, vmapped only over completion) is a real implementation contribution.

2. The conditional-vs-field estimand distinction. The explicit analysis that per-pixel normalization discards angular host density (radial-only estimand), that at K=1 the global Z cancels leaving only relative angular weighting, and that only at K>=2 the mixture weights become host fractions — this is a genuine conceptual clarification absent from the literature.

3. The matched-kernel smoothing operator making constant completeness an exact fixed point of the ratio, with no parametric roll-off. A clean technical refinement, though a refinement of DarkSirensStat's counts-based completeness, not a new idea.

STANDARD ELSEWHERE (do not claim)

- The in/out mixture decomposition: Gray/Gair 2020-2023, verbatim.
- Counts-vs-expected per-pixel completeness: Finke et al. 2021 cone/mask completeness — including its acknowledged clustering-absorption pathology.
- The legacy (1 + b*delta_g) missing-branch factor: linear-bias multiplicative completion, i.e., DarkSirensStat's multiplicative limit; Dalang & Baker (2310.08991, 2410.03275) already did the principled interpolation.
- Poisson-lognormal latent-Gaussian field with Laplace posterior and Jensen (sigma^2/2) corrections: textbook LGCP (Moller et al. 1998), BORG (Jasche & Wandelt), and specifically Leyde et al. for dark-siren completion. The posterior-mean logQ formula is standard lognormal-Cox algebra.
- Low-rank inducing-point GPs and sphere x radial kernels: Titsias 2009, Dutordoir 2020.
- Per-pixel KDE LOS priors: CHIMERA and gwcosmo 2023.

WHAT A REFEREE WILL SAY

The blunt problem: the construction fails its own design ideal, and your closure experiment proves it. Per-pixel counts-based C absorbs angular clustering (numerator per-pixel, denominator isotropic), so the missing branch anti-correlates with the true missing density (r=-0.43, slope -0.62) and the assembled prior cancels the catalog's clustering — the exact pathology imaging surveys structure their entire completeness methodology to avoid (injections/templates, never counts). Q cannot repair it because Q is fit to the same counts residual to C (slope 0.29 recovered vs 1.05 for the crude legacy factor). The identifiability caveat you document is the thinning degeneracy of Cox processes: a free selection surface and a free density field from one catalog is known to be unidentifiable. Worse, the uncertainty story — the most defensible novelty claim — is currently indefensible: 5% empirical coverage for gp3d Laplace members, fixed hyperparameters with ls_z ~30x below inducing-node resolution (fitted slope 0.04), and a shot-noise/Jensen-inflated radial mode. A competent referee will conclude the crude legacy delta_g factor outperforms the flagship GP machinery, and ask why the paper exists.

PUBLISHABLE CORE AND DEFENSIBLE FRAMING

The publishable core is NOT "a 3-D lognormal completion field" (Leyde owns that) and NOT counts-based completeness (Finke owns that, pathology included). It is:

(a) the first jointly-sampled, selection-consistent hierarchical dark-siren likelihood with a clustering-informed completion field and marginalized field uncertainty — framed as infrastructure/methodology, citing Leyde and Dalang as the completion pedigree;
(b) the estimand analysis (conditional vs field, what the inference actually constrains: dN_miss shape and N_obs:N_miss odds, host fractions at K>=2);
(c) the closure-experiment methodology itself — a quantitative demonstration that per-pixel counts-based C breaks the amount/placement split, which is a citable negative result against the DarkSirensStat-lineage construction.

To make (a) defensible you must first realize the owner's design ideal: make C a radial-only budget (sky-averaged, or template/injection-based per pixel) so all angular structure lives in Q; learn the GP lengthscales by marginal likelihood rather than fixing 50 Mpc; and either fix Laplace coverage (INLA-style corrections or MCMC benchmark) or drop the uncertainty claim. Publish the current C+Q stack as-is and the closure numbers become the referee's weapon instead of yours.
result.critique:
BREAKING PROPOSAL A

1. n0 coupling. C̄ = dN_obs_tot/(N_pix·n0·apix·(S g)) is exactly ∝ 1/n0, so dN_miss = n0·g·Q − (dN_obs_tot/N_pix)·Q. The sampled n0 now interacts with one global clip: for low-n0 draws C̄ pins at 1 over wide z-ranges, N_miss→0, and the likelihood is non-smooth in n0 precisely where the posterior of a weakly identified parameter lives. Per-pixel clipping engaged pixel-by-pixel and averaged smooth; the aggregate clip produces kinks. The optional isotonic constraint is ad hoc and biases if true selection is non-monotone.

2. Isotropy is fatal on GLADE+. Secular depth gradients (2MASS vs SDSS, Galactic plane) are order-unity and would be forced into a mean-one, clustering-lengthscale Q — the degeneracy re-entering, exactly as A admits. The sanctioned escape (stratified C̄_k) needs a depth proxy, i.e. per-region m_th — magnitudes. So A quietly depends on C's data channel to work on real catalogs, while each stratum shrinks the footprint and raises the sample-variance floor ~K-fold.

3. Per-z mean-one renormalization deletes any true monopole whose z-shape differs from g(z)(1+z)^δ. If C̄ is biased (anisotropy, sample variance), the compensating monopole Q would have carried is erased — the budget inherits C̄'s bias with no relief valve. Same for per-member renorm: budget uncertainty is assumed covered elsewhere, unverified.

4. Resolution floor: Q now targets full δ, but real 10–50 Mpc structure at M=192 collapses toward homogeneous (Burt et al.). Fails conservative, but the 800 Mpc closure mock cannot detect it — the validation passes while production gains evaporate.

BREAKING PROPOSAL B

1. It entrenches the defect every external literature thread flags: counts-based per-pixel C. delta_g multiplied onto (1−C) partially cancels the anti-correlation but is internally inconsistent (C absorbs +δ, lss reinstates it); its ceiling is the measured 0.77, not 1. P3 fixes gp3d representability but not the residual-target ceiling (the other cause of slope 0.29); only stretch-item P5 addresses that, so B's advertised gp3d slope ~1 is optimistic.

2. delta_g at production conditions: per-pixel KDE built from ~1 galaxy per smoothing volume, real correlation lengths 10–50 Mpc — b·δ_g is mostly shot noise; the max(·,0) rail clips deep voids; multiplicative completion overstates structure at low C (DarkSirensStat's own caveat).

3. P1's weights w_p = (1−C_p)·dN_exp use the biased per-pixel C, so the monopole is removed against wrong weights; "second-order" is asserted, not tested. P4's κ inflation is mock-calibrated and non-transferable.

Virtues: cheapest, reversible, per-item gates; P1/P2 are genuine architecture-independent bug fixes.

BREAKING PROPOSAL C

1. LF realism. The mock LF is Gaussian by construction; GLADE+ is a heterogeneous compilation with extinction, K-corrections, photometric errors, evolving Schechter shape, and no single m_lim. Per-pixel m_lim(p) estimation is itself the documented weak point (median-m_th caveats, arXiv:2502.14164). The Q-monopole alarm detects misspecification but the bias lands in the budget C_sel — the worst place for it.

2. Cosmology circularity. Magnitudes constrain θ only relative to the assumed DM(z): m = M + DM. Fixing θ̂ at fiducial cosmology inside an H0 inference re-imports the classic M*–H0 degeneracy; joint sampling or explicit h-scaling is a correctness requirement, not the optional refinement C presents it as.

3. Photo-z: "convolve base with S" conflates the fixed σ=0.05 KDE smoother with the survey's actual error law.

4. Largest diff: IO chain (generator, pixelate, catalogs/io), new module, base swap — most review surface. Same Q resolution floor as A.

SHARED RESIDUAL RISK. The closure mock (800 Mpc, isotropic selection, Gaussian LF) is friendly to all three; without anisotropic-depth and short-lengthscale variants, all three pass validation while diverging in production. And any newly sampled selection parameters must enter the selection integral mu(Lambda) (core.py self-calibration) or the prior reshapes penalty-free.

RANKING: Merged > C > A > B. A and C are the same architecture — isotropic (per-stratum) radial budget × mean-one full-field Q — differing only in the C estimator: aggregate counts (A) vs magnitudes (C). C's magnitude channel cures A's fatal anisotropy failure; A's counts-aggregate C̄ is the free cross-check on C's LF misspecification (already agreeing to 0.3% on the mock). B alone plateaus, but P1/P2 are needed under any architecture.

RECOMMENDED PATH (staged):
- Stage 0 (days): B-P2 depth-edge truncation; B-P1 per-z mean-one renorm with monopole recorded in provenance; CLI lengthscale/node knobs plus node-spacing hard error (B-P3, prerequisite of everything). Gates: budget closure <1%, no edge spike, lengthscale-recovery sweep.
- Stage 1 (~week): A's architecture behind an opt-in c_mode flag — aggregate C̄, full-δ Q target, empty pixels in the fit, fail-closed table provenance; legacy default bit-identical. Gates: missing-branch r>0.6 with positive slope ~1, voids recovered <0.5.
- Stage 2: C's two-step estimator for the budget where magnitudes exist — plumb APP_MAG, fit θ̂ per stratum, require |C_sel − counts-C̄| < 1% on the mock; stratified counts-C̄ stays as fallback and alarm. Sample θ (or h-scale) inside the GW likelihood before any real-data claim.
- Stage 3 (hardening): anisotropic-depth and 50 Mpc closure variants; marginal-likelihood hyperparameter grid with mixture-of-Laplace members (B-P4/C); scale M or move to spherical-harmonic features. The full joint fit remains validation-grade only.
